title: Layout Thrashing Batcher
subtopicTitle: Critical Rendering Path: Reflow vs Repaint
problemStatement: Implement `batchDOMOperations(reads, writes)` that separates an array of DOM measurement tasks (reads) and mutation tasks (writes), executing ALL reads first before executing any writes, preventing forced synchronous layout reflow.
interviewTrap: Alternating read-write-read-write inside a loop forces the browser to recalculate layout immediately on every iteration.

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Reflow recalculates geometry and layout tree (expensive). Repaint redraws pixels without changing geometry. Composite occurs on the GPU (transforms and opacity). Reading layout properties (`offsetWidth`, `scrollTop`) right after writing them forces synchronous layout thrashing.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Initialize execution context and environment records for Separating DOM Reads and Writes.
2. Execute logic adhering to ECMAScript standard specification.
3. Verify invariant boundaries and edge conditions.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In JavaScript engines (e.g. V8), Separating DOM Reads and Writes is optimized via inline caches, heap contexts, and bytecode translation.
edgeCasesHandled: Alternating read-write-read-write inside a loop forces the browser to recalculate layout immediately on every iteration.

verifiedRules: Adheres to ECMAScript runtime evaluation specifications.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What is Layout Thrashing (Forced Synchronous Layout)?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Layout Thrashing occurs when JavaScript alternately reads and writes DOM geometric properties in a loop (e.g. `element.style.width = x; const h = element.offsetHeight;`). Writing invalidates the layout tree; reading forces the browser engine to stop and execute synchronous recalculation of layout before continuing, dropping FPS to single digits.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Crucial web performance and browser engine question.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Which DOM properties trigger forced layout recalculation when read?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Reading geometric or scroll properties forces layout: `offsetWidth`, `offsetHeight`, `offsetTop`, `offsetLeft`, `scrollTop`, `scrollWidth`, `getBoundingClientRect()`, and `getComputedStyle()`. Browsers must flush pending layout queues to return accurate pixel values.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests knowledge of browser layout triggers.

realWorldUseCases.description: Coordinating UI animations across large teams by batching all DOM reads into `requestAnimationFrame` before scheduling DOM writes.
realWorldUseCases.companies: Wilson Page FastDOM, Google Chrome team
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: fastdom.measure(() => { const h = el.offsetHeight; fastdom.mutate(() => { el.style.height = h*2; }); });

howToExplain.opening: Layout thrashing is eliminated by separating DOM reads from DOM writes into distinct batches, preventing repetitive forced synchronous reflows.
keyPoints: Reading geometric properties flushes pending layout queues.
Alternating reads and writes causes multiple expensive layout passes per frame.
Batch all reads first (measure), then execute all writes (mutate).
Use requestAnimationFrame to synchronize mutations with display refresh.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Eliminating forced synchronous layouts is the #1 way to restore smooth 60fps animations in complex web apps.
analogies: A contractor measuring a house: measure all 10 rooms first with your tape measure, then cut all 10 boards at the saw, rather than measuring one room, cutting one board, and walking back 10 times.

commonMistakes.mistake: Reading offsetHeight inside a for loop that sets style.top.
commonMistakes.why: Forces N synchronous layout passes, turning an O(N) loop into an O(N^2) CPU bottleneck.
commonMistakes.correct: Read all heights into an array first, then apply all top styles in a second pass.

followUpDeepDive.question: How do modern CSS containment properties (contain: layout paint) help layout performance?
followUpDeepDive.answer: `contain: layout` tells the browser layout engine that the element's internal layout has zero influence on the rest of the page, scoping reflow recalculations strictly to that subtree.
